kernels.method: Five fixed geometries at 256 and 400 image cells per side, both phases. Fresh gradient modules per case isolate backend decisions. First-call timings include calibration, alternate previous/current order and exclude module loading and comparisons. Four subsequent rotating policy orders use 16 calls per timer after warmup. Every result must match the previous JavaScript gradient exactly. Times are milliseconds per call.
kernels.firstCallTimerScope: Includes polygon indexing, backend calibration and its internal equality checks. Only module imports and the benchmark's external output comparisons are excluded.

hunodan.criteria: Each prepare + solve + validate + export <=10 seconds; independent error <= that case’s validated release error, plus at most 1 percentage point for an identical pair; unchanged geometry, strict paper and substantial feature checks. Decode and independent external replay are timed separately.

weighted.method: Fresh automatic mask solves. Frames fixed before fitting. Checker strategy replaces the band; weighted strategy retains the original mask with zero band weights. Exported controls are independently rendered with resvg. Geometric and paper checks remain enabled. Variants swap both colours, translate by one source pixel in both axes with background fill, or alter only zero-weight pixels; the protected frame stays fixed.

weightedReplay.note: Fresh process replay of the timing failure, after the full perturbation batch. Does not replace the failed timing in the original batch.

timingDiagnostic.reason: One elapsed-time failure; protected-mask error is unchanged. CPU time is substantially shorter than wall time, with no new gradient calibration. This suggests a scheduling delay or pause contributed, without establishing the cause of all timing differences.

limitations: First-call calibration timers exclude module loading and output comparisons; shared dependencies and browser JIT can remain warm between cases. They are not cold-browser startup timings.
Exact equality is checked on recorded inputs, not proved for every future geometry or runtime.
All whole-solve comparisons are separate runs, not interleaved trials. Whole-solve speed and fitting results remain hardware-, runtime- and deadline-dependent.
Four milliseconds is a batch measurement target; a single call can exceed it. Frozen clocks stop at the 16-call limit.
A backend chosen for one geometry may not be optimal for every subsequent geometry in its workload bucket.
The guarded discrete paper model does not certify tear resistance or physical assembly.
